subject.title: RFC: Distributed Agent Runtime — separate control plane from agent compute

question: Should OpenClaw pursue a core Gateway/control-plane plus per-agent runtime split, and what should the first supported milestone own?
rationale: The request changes architecture, security boundaries, lifecycle behavior, and upgrade expectations across Gateway, agents, channels, and provider execution, so automation cannot choose the product direction safely.

options.title: Approve a phased core split
options.body: Define a narrow first milestone covering local runtime protocol, worker identity, lifecycle commands, session ownership, and compatibility tests before expanding to remote or autoscaled workers.

options.title: Route scaling to external/plugin surfaces first
options.body: Keep core Gateway lean and use plugin or deployment integrations for orchestration until a missing core API is proven by narrower issues such as #82017.

options.title: Close as out of scope
options.body: Reject first-class runtime separation for now and direct HA/autoscaling needs to external deployment patterns and narrower issue-specific work.

recommendation.title: Approve a phased core split
recommendation.body: Define a narrow first milestone covering local runtime protocol, worker identity, lifecycle commands, session ownership, and compatibility tests before expanding to remote or autoscaled workers.

likelyOwner.reason: They are tied to the adjacent worker-runtime isolation experiment and broader runtime architecture history, making them the best available owner for the product-direction decision.
